annotations.shape: hand-written bytes (tools/write_raw_fixtures.py holds them as typed literals): a single text/plain part declared base64 whose payload is a base64 run cut mid-quantum with no padding -- a transfer encoding that cannot decode
annotations.provenance: the bytes are frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS and checked by tests/test_fixtures.py; a generator would be encoding the assumption under test (D11's raw hand-written set), and the measured spike (b02) shows stdlib's decode and its defect list disagreeing on exactly these inputs
annotations.phase_numbering: the design document's phases: 0 = the Phase 0 skeleton walker (spans, decode chain, accounted regions, gaps), 1 = the Phase 1 parser (header projection, body views, attachment manifest), 2 = routing and statuses, 3 = threading and time evidence
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the design rules (D2/D3/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: the part is the whole message; headers_span includes the closing empty line; the body span is the base64 run with its final line ending (the message ends at EOF)
annotations.expected_gaps: body.decode_fallback_used (D9): the declared transfer encoding cannot be applied to these bytes and the payload is kept verbatim, never partially decoded
annotations.not_yet_labelled: the status the Phase 2 parser will give this body (the closed nine-member vocabulary), views (phase 1), thread edges and TimeEvents (phase 3)
annotations.the_declarative_layer: the expected decode chain here is the raw chain, not a readable message: used_cte is null because the declared base64 run never produced bytes -- see labels.undetermined for what the design does not say about that state

value: the design records used_cte beside declared_cte but never says what used_cte is when the declared transfer decoding cannot run: this label writes null (no transfer decoding was used) where Turn 0.2's walker also records null, and asks the design to settle null versus an explicit identity verdict, because a reader that saw used_cte null could equally conclude the part was never transfer-decoded at all
